_comment_variant: HYDRA Variant H — 0DTE SPX LONG STRANGLE (Tompkins / Theta Profits). The structural MIRROR of variant G: the same two legs, the opposite sign. G SELLS an OTM call + an OTM put; H BUYS them. That inverts everything: NET DEBIT not credit, LONG gamma, SHORT theta, and max loss = the premium paid (defined by construction, so there is NO stop loss and no stop machinery at all). It is the only long-gamma strategy in the fleet — A/B/C/F/G all sell premium and D/E are net debit but theta-POSITIVE — which is the entire reason to run it: to MEASURE whether long gamma hedges the short-gamma book's bad days. STATUS: Step 1 scaffold per docs/NEW_STRATEGY_PLAYBOOK.md — registered, dry-run-LOCKED, and INERT (no entry logic implemented). The entry/exit knobs below are PLACEHOLDERS for Steps 3–5 and are not read by any code yet. Claims from the source (80% WR, +50–100%) are NOT believed — see docs/LONG_STRANGLE_STRATEGY_SPECIFICATION.md §1.
_comment_credentials: IBKR OAuth credentials are loaded from systemd $CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY on the VM, or env vars in dev. Not in this file.

strategy.name: long_strangle
strategy._comment_commission: IBKR all-in SPX cost ~$1.15/leg/contract — see config_variant_c.json's comment for the full breakdown.
strategy._comment_entry_times: The source says only 'he generally enters near the market open' — a SINGLE entry, not a grid (one slot is the faithful reading; kept as a list for shape-compatibility with the base). ⚠️ 09:45 IS OUR CHOICE, NOT HIS NUMBER, and the reason is evidence rather than preference: the ATM STRADDLE PRICE IS THE INPUT TO THE STRIKE CHOICE, so an unreliable opening quote does not merely delay the entry, it picks the WRONG STRIKES. On 2026-09-22 the armed paper smoke aborted TWICE on absent SPXW quotes at 09:29:31 and 09:30:40, and the same check passed cleanly at 09:35 and again at 09:35 on 09-23 (bid 8.1 / ask 8.2, first poll, no re-poll needed) — the post-mortem's conclusion was 'timing is the primary fix'. 09:45 sits comfortably past that instability. REVISIT once the RTH probe shows how early the straddle quote is actually trustworthy; if it is stable by 09:35 this should move earlier, because 'near the open' is his wording and 15 minutes is a loose reading of it.
strategy._comment_delta: PLACEHOLDER (Step 4) and LIKELY WRONG AS A MECHANISM. The source does NOT pick strikes by delta — it uses spot ± the options-market EXPECTED MOVE, then checks both premiums are 'reasonably similar' for skew. target_delta is retained only so base-class code paths that read it do not see a missing key. Step 4 must decide WHICH expected move (F computes a VIX-implied one at ghauri_strategy.py:324; the source means the ATM straddle) — that choice IS the strategy.
strategy._comment_safety_caps: Conservative sizing at 1c while this variant is dry-run-locked and under initial observation — matches variant A/F's ORDER-006 defaults.
strategy._comment_mkt046: 2026-08-28: same disable as B/C/F (see config_variant_b.json's comment + bots/hydra/__init__.py version history) — MKT-046's 10s wait isn't part of any of these strategies' original research; disabling here matches that reasoning rather than G's own stop history, which is essentially nonexistent (dry-run-locked, first live day 2026-08-28, one real stop so far — see the 2026-08-28 audit). Zero real-money risk either way. Note: this is the confirmation TIMING only, unrelated to the separate close-cost-estimator bug fixed the same day.
strategy._comment_whipsaw: DISABLED (null) ON PURPOSE, 2026-09-23 — and this is the single most important config line in the file. The anti-whipsaw filter skips an entry when the intraday range exceeds 1.75x the expected move. For a premium SELLER (A/B/C/F/G) that is protective: a wild day is when a short position gets hurt. H is the opposite — a wide range is the day it EXISTS FOR, so the inherited gate would systematically skip its best sessions and we would be measuring 'the source's strategy minus its winners'. The source specifies no such filter. Set it back to 1.75 only if the dry run shows H losing money specifically on wide-range days, which would be a genuine surprise.
strategy._comment_fomc: fomc_announcement_skip=FALSE on purpose, and for the OPPOSITE reason to G's. G trades announcement days while carrying undefined risk, which is the outlier flagged in GO_LIVE_MASTER §2-ter. A long strangle's risk is capped at the debit, and an FOMC announcement is precisely the large-move event it exists to capture — skipping those would remove the days most likely to show whether the hedge thesis holds. Revisit at promotion.
strategy._comment_fomc_t1: DISABLED 2026-09-23. The day AFTER a Fed announcement is frequently a large-move day, which is exactly what a long strangle wants — and the source specifies no FOMC handling at all. A/B/C black it out because an unresolved post-Fed drift hurts a short position; that reasoning does not transfer to a long one. Paired with fomc_announcement_skip=false below, H trades both the announcement and the day after, deliberately.

vix_regime._comment: DISABLED 2026-09-23. The source specifies no VIX-regime behaviour of any kind, and for H the block is INERT anyway: it overwrites min_call_credit / min_put_credit / call_stop_buffer / put_stop_buffer, and H uses NO credits and NO stops. Its only live effect was cosmetic and misleading — _effective_total_entry_count() estimates from max(max_entries)=2 before VIX is known, so the heartbeat read 'Entries: 0/2' for a strategy with exactly ONE entry slot. The arrays are left in place so the shape is unchanged and re-enabling is one boolean, but nothing reads them while enabled=false.

strategy._comment_no_stops: DELIBERATELY ABSENT: call_stop_buffer / put_stop_buffer / min_buying_power_per_strangle. A long strangle's maximum loss is the debit paid, known before entry, so there is nothing to stop out of and no margin to reserve. No GUARD-FLOOR, no A2 %-of-width, no buffer decay. If a stop knob ever appears in this file, something has been copied in by mistake.
strategy._comment_long_strangle: ⚠️ sizing_for_zero_max_loss RAISED 500 -> 1200 on 2026-09-23 BECAUSE $500 MEANT H COULD NEVER TRADE. The RTH probe measured a real 1-contract debit of $775 at SPX 7724, so size_for_zero(500, 775) = 0 contracts and every session would have skipped — collecting nothing, which defeats the only reason the variant exists. $500 was OUR number, not the source's: he trades SPY, where the same strangle costs ~$115, so his own sizing would buy several contracts for $500. His COST CAP scaled to SPX is ~$1,145/contract, so 1200 keeps one contract affordable in normal conditions while staying close to his ceiling. THIS IS A RISK-APPETITE DIAL AND IT IS REVERSIBLE — lower it to stop H trading, raise it to let it size up. ALL of these are read by Steps 4-5. profit_target_pct_of_debit is the exit; profit_target_pct_of_debit_iv_expanding (+100%) is UNREACHABLE until iv_percentile_source is wired, which is stated rather than silently defaulted. profit_target_confirm_seconds is 0 ON PURPOSE and is the one place the playbook's own Step-5 instruction is deliberately inverted: a breach-persistence window protects a STOP (which fires on an adverse spike) but systematically gives back a long-gamma PROFIT TARGET (which fires on a favourable spike, and those revert). The guard against a phantom target here is quote quality, not elapsed time. The knob exists at a non-default value so the dry run can falsify that reasoning. expected_move_source SELECTS WHICH STRATEGY RUNS — 'straddle' (source-faithful, ~22pt on 2026-09-22) and 'vix' (F's formula, ~71pt on the same day) disagree by ~3x and there is deliberately NO FALLBACK between them: if the configured one can't be computed the entry is skipped, because silently substituting the other would blend two strategies into one unseparable series. iv_percentile_filter_enabled is now TRUE (2026-09-23) and runs off VIX history from market_ticks — the source SPECIFIES an IV-percentile <35% filter and running without it was the larger infidelity. It had been off on the reasoning that we store no option-IV history; that was too absolutist. The source is a retail trader reading 'IV percentile' off a broker platform, and for SPX that number comes from index-option implied vol, which is what VIX IS. ⚠️ CAVEAT TO CARRY: VIX is 30-DAY implied vol, not the IV of the specific 0DTE contracts being bought — they move together but are different points on the term structure, and every skip this produces says so in its reason string. ⚠️ SECOND CAVEAT: as of wiring the sample is ~93 trading days spanning VIX 13.95-22.59, i.e. NO high-vol regime, so a '35th percentile' here is ranked against a calm-only history. It widens as the record grows. profit_target_pct_of_debit_iv_expanding (+100%) now runs too, and requires BOTH conditions the source states — cheap AND rising — because a low percentile alone is the ENTRY filter, not the exit rule. skew_tolerance_pct 35 remains OURS: the source performs the check but never quantifies it ('reasonably similar').

long_strangle._comment_cost_cap: THE SOURCE'S COST CAP, added 2026-09-23. He will not pay more than ~$1.15/share for a SPY strangle (~$1.30-1.40 QQQ) — a QUALITY filter, distinct from sizing_for_zero_max_loss: that decides HOW MANY to buy, this refuses to OVERPAY in the first place. ⚠️ THE PORT IS OURS: he trades SPY/QQQ, we chose SPX. $1.15 on a ~$775 SPY is 0.1483% of spot, so the same fraction on SPX is ~$11.50/share ~= $1,150/contract. Expressed as a PERCENTAGE so it tracks the index rather than going stale. At 1 contract with a $500 loss limit, sizing-for-zero binds first and this never fires — implemented anyway because the two rules are independent and raising the loss limit later must not silently drop his.
long_strangle._comment_iv_percentile_min_history_days: SAMPLE-SIZE FLOOR, added 2026-09-23. iv_percentile() had no minimum: with one prior day it returns 0.0 or 100.0 — a number with the exact shape of a percentile, the full authority of one, and no information in it. Below this floor the gate now returns 'unknown' and SKIPS, never passes. Set to 60 rather than the 252 above because the live-seat DB currently holds ~94 days: demanding the full year would block H for months and produce the empty dataset the sizing fix already had to rescue it from, while 60 is enough for a percentile to mean something. The skip reason and the log line both state the window ACTUALLY used whenever it is short of the lookback, and iv_percentile_n is stored per row, so no reading can later be mistaken for the one-year percentile the lookback asks for. RISK DIAL: raise it to demand a longer history (stricter, fewer entries), lower it to admit more.
long_strangle._comment_max_debit_pct_of_spot: His cost cap, and it needs NO change for the SPY switch because it is already expressed relative to spot: 0.1483% of SPY 765 = $1.13/share = ~$113/contract, which IS his stated ~$1.15/share SPY cap. On SPX the same number gave ~$1,143/contract. Spot-relative was the right shape and it ported for free.
long_strangle._comment_sizing_for_zero_max_loss: $200 — the most H can lose in a day, which for this structure is simply the debit it paid. SET TO AGREE WITH contracts_per_entry:1 RATHER THAN BE RESCUED BY IT. It was $1,200 (a number chosen so ONE $775 SPX contract was affordable); after the 2026-09-24 SPY switch that same limit let the sizing rule compute ~10-15 contracts, and only the fleet cap held the actual position at 1. A limit 10x looser than the cap that binds is a trap: raise contracts_per_entry later and the position jumps by 10x that nobody decided. At $200, the rule and the cap both say 1 at a realistic ~$77-113 SPY debit, so the config states the intent instead of hiding it. WHY 1 WHILE MEASURING: H is judged in pnl_pct_of_debit, so the contract count scales dollars and changes NOTHING about what is learned — 1 and 10 give identical percentages, win rate and peak-vs-exit gap. A larger count only inflates phantom dry-run P&L that can later be mistaken for something real. A/F/G all run 1c for the same reason. RISK DIAL: raise both this and contracts_per_entry together when H has a record worth sizing up.
long_strangle._comment_min_buying_power_per_long_stran: Kept at the loss limit: long options are fully paid, so the capital required IS the debit.

strategy._comment_underlying_symbol: SPY, NOT SPX — changed 2026-09-24 to match the source. Jeff Tompkins trades SPY, and the spec's own §1 records that the source DOES NOT RESTRICT the underlying; SPX was OUR choice 'to match the rest of the fleet'. That choice was not free: the identical strangle costs ~$115 on SPY and ~$775 on SPX, which is exactly how sizing_for_zero_max_loss=$500 came to permit ZERO contracts and would have produced an empty dataset. On SPY his own sizing rule behaves as he describes it — a $1,200 limit buys ~10 contracts, not 1 or 0. VERIFIED 2026-09-24 03:0x ET before switching: SPY quotes real-time (6509='Rp', bid 764.81 / ask 764.91) where SPX was frozen; the 0DTE chain for 2026-09-24 resolves with 329 strikes at $1 spacing near the money; and variant E already trades SPY, so the plumbing is proven. ⚠️ SPY options are AMERICAN and PHYSICALLY settled: an ITM leg held to expiry becomes 100 shares/contract. That does not change dry-run P&L (intrinsic - debit is still the correct economic value) but it is a GO-LIVE PRECONDITION — see H_GOLIVE_SCOPE_AND_AUDIT HG-11.
strategy._comment_trading_class: SPY's own weeklies. SPXW was the SPX 0DTE class; the SPY equivalent is just 'SPY', which lists daily expirations Monday-Friday.
strategy._comment_strike_increment: $1 near the money, measured off the live chain 2026-09-24 (755-775 all present). This is the number that makes the old hardcoded 25.0 snap tolerance dangerous — see max_snap_distance.
strategy._comment_max_snap_distance: LEFT NULL ON PURPOSE so the tolerance is DERIVED from the live chain's own near-the-money spacing (chain_snap_cap: 2.5x the median gap -> 12.5 on SPX, 2.5 on SPY). The previous hardcoded 25.0 was half the widest far-OTM SPXW gap: correct on SPX, and on SPY's $1 chain it would have authorised snapping TWENTY-FIVE strikes while still placing, logging and looking like an ordinary entry. Set a number here only to pin a value deliberately.

long_salvage._comment: Strangle has no long legs to salvage (long_call_strike/long_put_strike are always 0.0) — short_only_stop stays false (close-both-legs default), same as every other variant. Not meaningfully exercised by this strategy either way.
